#804. Mariah Carey Claps Back at Online Criticism After Recent Performances

Mariah Carey appeared to address online speculation about her health during a performance in Rio de Janeiro on Nov. 21.

All Mariah Carey wants for Christmas, is to put this topic to rest.

As the queen of the holiday season performed at Farmasi Arena in Rio de Janeiro Nov. 21, she appeared to address speculation surrounding her health following her latest concerts.

“By the way, don’t believe everything you read online,” Carey said in a video shared by fans on social media after the show. “Don’t be making me mad, now.”

The “We Belong Together” singer’s comments shortly followed fan speculation that she was going through some sort of health battle due to the blocking in her recent shows.

“Is Mariah Carey choosing to perform as stiff as possible, or is something going on with her health?” a fan wrote on X earlier this month. “She is 57 and needs assistance to even walk around the stage.”

Another responded to a separate video of Carey—mom to 15-year-old twins Moroccan and Monroe with ex Nick Cannon—appearing to struggle to walk in high heels, “If her health really is bad then she needs to take time off and work on herself.”

But some of Carey’s Lambily quickly hopped in to defend her, even before the Grammy winner herself stepped in. As one fan joked in response to the speculation, “She’s still defrosting!!”

The comment, of course, references Carey’s reign as the queen of the festive season—but she has at least begun to thaw this Christmas by kicking off her latest tour.

“Thank you São Paulo!!” Carey wrote in a Nov. 18 post on social media, alongside picture that featured her decked out in Santa outfits. “What an incredible way to kick off my Christmastime Tour.”

And while Carey has become synonymous for her holiday hit—which was only just this year dethroned as the longest charting Billboard hit by Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas”—she has previously emphasized that it isn’t a fluke and she “really, truly loves the holidays.”

“It’s not fake,” she told Good Morning America of her seasonal spirit in 2023, noting that she loves touring during the winter to ensure her fans have “the merriest of Christmases.”

Even 32 years after she put out the record, Carey isn’t surprised it remains her chart-topper, either. After all, fans being obsessed with it was the point. As she put of writing it back in the early 1990s, “My goal was to do something timeless.”

For more fascinating facts about Carey, keep reading…

1. Mariah Carey was born on March 27, 1970 (we think) to Alfred Roy Carey and Patricia Hickey, who'd been disowned by her family for marrying a man of African-American and Afro-Venezuelan descent. They divorced when Carey was 3.

2. Her name comes from the song "They Call the Wind Maria" from the 1951 Broadway musical Paint Your Wagon. Though it isn't spelled the same, it is pronounced the same.

3. When she was young, her family, which includes two older siblings, was subjected to racist attacks because of her parents' interracial marriage. Their dogs were poisoned and a car was blown up.

"That was the beginning of a nightmare," Patricia told Oprah Winfrey during a 1999 interview with her daughter. "When we were eating one night, someone fired a shot through the window. Luckily, none of the children were in the room."

4. While attending Harborfields High School in Greenlawn, New York, she earned the nickname Mirage because of how often she skipped class. According to her unauthorized 2001 biography by Marc Shapiro, Carey's truancy was of great concern for guidance counselor John Garvey.

"You could talk to her until you were blue in the face, and it didn't do any good," Garvey said in the book. "When you talked to her about it, she'd let you know it wasn't that important in her life because she was going to be a rock star." Carey's response? "I don't blame them for trying to encourage me to do better scholastically because they never saw me sing."

5. While recording her third album Music Box, she and Columbia Records head Tommy Mottola began dating. They tied the knot in a lavish ceremony in June 5, 1993. They eventually separated in 1997, with Carey citing his controlling nature and growing creative differences at the catalyst for their relationship's deterioration.

Carey opened up about the relationship on her E! reality series, Mariah's World, saying "I was with someone at the time that had a lot of control over my life. He was older than me by a lot and had a lot of power and he wanted me to remain away from most people, like sequestered. I had to get permission to leave [the house]…I never thought I would get out of there."

6. The first song she ever composed was written while she was still in high school. Called "Here We Go 'Round Again," Carey has described the track, which was featured on her four-song demo tape, as having a Motown vibe.

7. After graduating high school, she moved into a one-bedroom apartment in Manhattan that she shared with four other female students. She worked as a waitress and a coat check girl while also studying cosmetology—all while pursuing her dreams of a music career.

8. At the age of 2, Carey stunned her mom, a vocal coach and occasional opera singer, by imitating her operatic singing. She began taking singing lessons at 4, developing a voice that would span five octaves—a nearly superhuman feat.

9. After meeting rising pop singer Brenda K. Starr, Carey tagged along as her new friend attended a Christmas party hosted by CBS Records. Starr convinced her to bring along her demo tape, which made its way into the hands of the head of Columbia Records, Mottola. All it took was two songs to convince Mottola to sign her.

10. Carey's debut eponymous album was released on June 12, 1990. She earned two Grammys following its release, including one for Best New Artist, and it made her the first musical act since the Jackson 5 to have their first four singles reach number one.

11. Carey's had a life-long affection for Marilyn Monroe and, in 1999, she paid over $600,000 for the icon's white baby grand piano when it came up for auction at Christie's.

12. After meeting Nick Cannon on the set of her music video for "Bye Bye" in 2008, she began dating the comedian. Within two months, they got married, tying the knot on April 30 in a secret ceremony in the Bahamas. They split in 2014.

13. Though she suffered a miscarriage shortly after marrying Cannon, the couple would welcome twins Moroccan and Monroe in 2011. Monroe was named after Carey's idol, Marilyn Monroe, while Moroccan was named after the décor in the room where his father proposed to his mother.

14. In 2008, Carey got herself into some hot water when she performed in a New Year's Eve concert for the family of Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi. She would later claim to "feel horrible and embarrassed to have participated in the event," with her rep Cindi Berger promising in March 2011 that royalties for her upcoming song "Save The Day" would be donated to charities that create awareness for human rights issues. The song was eventually released in 2020.

15. In 2001, after a bizarre appearance on TRL that involved her showing up unannounced, pushing an ice cream cart, and stripping off her clothes, she spent two weeks recovering in a Connecticut mental hospital, citing extreme exhaustion for her breakdown.

She later revealed in 2018 that she had been diagnosed with bipolar II disorder at the time, but kept her diagnosis private. "I'm just in a really good place right now, where I'm comfortable discussing my struggles with bipolar II disorder," she told People at the time. "I'm hopeful we can get to a place where the stigma is lifted from people going through anything alone. It can be incredibly isolating. It does not have to define you and I refuse to allow it to define me or control me."

16. Just months after her stay in the institution, Carey released Glitter into the world. The film and its soundtrack were such bombs that they prompted Virgin Records to buy her out of her record deal for $50 million. She would sign a contract with Island Records in early 2002, launching the record label MonarC in the process.

17. Glitter isn't the only film Carey has appeared in over the years. She earned some pretty great reviews for her work as a social worker in friend Lee Daniels' award-winning 2009 film Precious. In 2013, she appeared in another Daniels' film, The Butler, playing Hattie Pearl, the mother of the film's titular butler, Cecil Gaines (played by Forest Whitaker).

18. Until 2017 "One Sweet Day," Carey's song with Boyz II Men, was the longest-running number one song in history, with 16 weeks spent atop the Billboard Hot 100 in 1995-96. It shared the honor with Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee's "Despacito," featuring Justin Bieber, for a time before Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" surpassed it in the summer of 2019.

19. According to Page Six, Carey's two Jack Russell terriers only fly first class and each with their own respective staff member. Why? Because they apparently loathe one another.

20. Following a career resurgence with the 2005 release of The Emancipation of Mimi, Carey begun lending her name and likeness to endorsement deals for the first time in her career, beginning with ads for Intel Centrino personal computers. In 2006, after signing a contract with Gillette's "Legs of a Goddess" campaign, Carey reportedly insured her legs for $1 billion.

21. After meeting him through her longtime pal, director Brett Ratner, at a movie premiere in Aspen, Colo., Carey became engaged to Australian businessman James Packer in January 2016.

The billionaire, who formed the joint production company RatPac Entertainment with Ratner, proposed with a 35-carat ring. The engagement was called off by October, as both insinuated the relationship ended because of the other's issues.

22. Carey's classic 1994 album Merry Christmas has sold over 18 million copies worldwide, making it the best-selling Christmas album of all time. 25 years after its release, in late December of 2019, her beloved single "All I Want for Christmas Is You" hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for the first time, breaking several records (including longest trip to the top) in the process. While extending her record as the solo artist with the most No. 1 singles on the Hot 100, the achievement also made her the only artist in history to have a No. 1 song in four consecutive decades.

23. Her godmother is Patti LaBelle, and the R&B icon has admitted to slapping her goddaughter around back in the day.

24. After Packer, Carey quickly rebounded with backup dancer Bryan Tanaka, the early stages of their relationship captured by Mariah's World cameras.

25. She does not know Jennifer Lopez. So stop asking her.

#803. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland & Wales to host 2035 Women's World Cup

Spain beat England 1-0 to win the 2023 World Cup

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.

It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.

The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.

The tournament will consist of 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.

The 'All Together' bid included a proposal to use 19 venues, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

Monday's special meeting of Fifa's Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

The news comes on the same day the UK government announced a vision for one million more girls to play, watch or be in leadership roles in sport by the time the tournament takes place.

Hosting World Cup means decade of excitement - Weir

Fifa announces UK will host 2035 Women's World Cup

England failed to win the right to host the men's World Cups in 2006 and 2018, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for the 2030 tournament was abandoned.

But England and Scotland hosted matches at the men's Euros in 2021, and England staged the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.

England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the men's European Championship in 2028.

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.

"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations."

The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

If Manchester United's proposed new Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it would still be considered in its current form.

Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland.

Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.

A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.

Fifa is yet to decide whether all four co-hosts will qualify automatically.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff is one of two Welsh venues, along with the Cardiff City Stadium

The participation of women and girls in football has risen by 2.3m since the Women's European Championship was held in England in 2022.

However, women remain significantly underrepresented in leadership positions.

Only a quarter of chief executive, chair or performance director roles in major UK sports are held by women and only 12% of sports federations are led by a female.

Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "This is a proud day for Welsh football.

"We've put forward Wrexham and Cardiff as host cities, and it's exciting to think what a World Cup could bring to both cities and the communities around them.

"In Llunio Cymru - our 10-year strategy - we've set ourselves the ambition of reaching the knockout stages in 2035. Some of the players who could take us there are learning the game at clubs across Wales today. Our job is to make sure that wherever a girl grows up in Wales, she can find a team close to home, have a coach who helps her develop and see a route to the Cymru shirt."

Irish Football Association chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country".

"Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that," he added.

Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".

He added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come."

Fifa's evaluation, published earlier this month, rated the bid 4.3 out of five. Its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".

That is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.

The bid evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.

"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."

#802. Glens boss Ferguson apologises after seven-game ban

Duncan Ferguson jointly holds the record for the most red cards in Premier League history with eight.

Glentoran manager Duncan Ferguson has been suspended for seven games following his red card in the side's 3-2 defeat by Cliftonville last week.

The former Everton striker was dismissed for how he addressed match officials after believing the Reds' opener at Solitude should have been ruled out for a foul in the build-up.

The 1995 FA Cup winner arrived at the Oval in October and has so far won one, drawn two and lost one of his four games in charge.

"I want to apologise to the match officials for my behaviour on Friday night," said the former Forest Green Rovers and Inverness Caledonian Thistle boss.

"I was frustrated by what happened on the pitch and let my emotions get the better of me. I went too far in the way I expressed that frustration towards the officials, and I should have handled the situation better."

"I accept the suspension and I'll learn from what happened. My focus now is on the players, the staff and the work we've got to do together, both on and off the pitch."

The sanction will start with Tuesday night's hosting of Larne in the Bet McLean Cup, a competition in which the east Belfast outfit have been beaten finalists the past two seasons.

Even should the Glens progress to the quarter-finals of the competition expected to take place next month, Ferguson's ban would still include the eagerly anticipated Boxing Day visit from fierce rivals Linfield.

#801. Barnet forward Noel-Williams charged with rape

Isiah Noel-Williams has been remanded in custody

League Two footballer Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged with rape.

Noel-Williams, who plays for League Two side Barnet, has been charged with three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault by penetration, Hertfordshire Police said.

The 23-year-old, of High Oaks, St Albans, was remanded in custody following a hearing at Hatfield Magistrates' Court on Saturday.

In a statement, the club said it was "co-operating fully with authorities" and would determine further action "in due course".

Noel-Williams has also been charged with one count of engaging in sexual communication with a child, and one count of supplying a controlled (Class B) drug, police added.

In a statement, the London club said: "Barnet FC can confirm that first-team player Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged and remanded in custody as part of a police investigation by Hertfordshire Constabulary.

"The club is co-operating fully with the authorities and will determine any further action in due course.

"As this is now a matter for the courts, the club will not be making any further comment."

Noel-Williams, who previously played for Hemel Hempstead Town, Kettering Town, Matlock Town, Harrow Borough and Cheshunt, joined Barnet in June.

#800. Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe was working as a spy for China could have profound implications for the $5 trillion (€4.47 trillion) company.

The Financial Times first reported on Huang's affair with Alice H., an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia, which has been suspected of trying to circumvent export controls to get advanced Nvidia chips into China.

The newspaper reported that the US government and its intelligence community believe she was recruited as a spy by China's Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

US government officials drafted a memo about the allegations shortly before US President Donald Trump traveled to Beijing for a summit with Xi Jinping in May.

Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese spy has exposed him and the company to criticism that it may have allowed China to obtain valuable trade secrets as Beijing tries to gain an edge in the race to develop advanced AI models.

Nvidia is initiating an investigation led by independent board members and an external law firm. It said in a statement that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."

"The board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders," the company said Sunday. "While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board's inquiry will examine all available information."

The company's shares fell in early trading on Monday.

While US intelligence officials have not commented publicly on the claims, Trump — with whom Jensen Huang has a close relationship — has backed the Nvidia boss.

"He's an honorable guy," said Trump. "I have not spoken to him ​about it. I just know he's a ​fine person, but you never know what is going on. I hope everything's fine."

Tim Culpan, an Asia tech reporter who has covered Nvidia and Huang closely for years, told DW that while Nvidia's fundamental strengths as a company remain in place, Huang is hugely personally damaged by the story.

"They're still going to make great chips and they're going to sell them to millions of customers around the world who want the best AI chips in the world," he said.

"His opinion is going to carry a lot less weight now. And that, in the long term, will flow through to Nvidia and Nvidia's own corporate interests. So it won't be immediate. It's really a fact that he doesn't have the sway or the power that he might have had one week ago simply through this."

Richard Windsor, a tech analyst and the founder of research company Radio Free Mobile, said the news could be very serious for Nvidia given how much the company has revolved around Huang for decades.

"This problem is particularly acute because Jensen Huang is very hands-on, meaning that the key decisions that led to its success were ultimately taken by him and because there is no obvious successor," he said.

"I suspect we are about to find out just how much the market thinks that the company is dependent on its iconic founder and CEO."

Nvidia and Huang's attitude toward China and potential Chinese customers has been a bone of contention with US intelligence officials — despite Huang's close relationship with Trump.

Huang has repeatedly lobbied Trump to ease restrictions on the sale of Nvidia chips to China. A 2025 export control deal heavily curbed sales, but Trump subsequently permitted the export of older H200 Nvidia chips to China in return for the US government receiving a cut of the sales.

However, that deal has been complicated and bogged down by Washington's strict export-license review. China has also initiated import controls, despite strong demand from Chinese companies. China lacks access to the most advanced AI-capable chips. Beijing wants to develop its own alternatives but has struggled to catch up.

Huang has argued that Chinese dependence on Nvidia's chips would prevent rivals such as Huawei from catching up and boosting China's ambitions to dominate AI supply chains.

However, that argument has been dismissed by many US intelligence officials. They fear that unlimited Chinese access to the most advanced Nvidia chips would boost China's domestic AI sector, lead to its AI models catching up with the leading US models and see the chips being used in Chinese military applications.

The US-China rivalry has become a central theme in the global AI story, with both countries seeking to gain an upper hand in the technology. Leading US AI executives such as Anthropic's Dario Amodei have argued that US AI companies can't afford to take a prolonged pause to allow safety standards in AI to catch up, if they're going to prevent Chinese firms from gaining an advantage.

Washington's central fear over Huang's affair is that it could have led to Beijing obtaining vital trade secrets or other key information about how Nvidia makes its most advanced chips.

Windsor thinks Huang will survive the "severe test" due to his importance to the company. He also cast doubt on the extent to which Beijing and its leading tech firms have learned from Nvidia's chips, pointing to China's own chip ambitions and commitment to have its firms buy its own semiconductors.

"I am far from convinced that Chinese AI has materially benefited from technology or illicit chip imports that it gained from Nvidia," he said.

The news comes at a particularly challenging moment for Nvidia, which has benefited massively from the AI boom thanks to its position as the leading maker of cutting-edge semiconductors needed for AI applications.

Nvidia's valuation has soared dramatically in recent years as companies rushed to buy its chips, becoming the world's first $5 trillion company in October 2025.

However, doubts over the sustainability of the $9 trillion capital expenditure AI boom have sparked a major sell-off in stocks related to the boom in recent weeks. The Democrats' sweeping victories in the US midterms have added to the doubts, given the strength of voter opposition to data center construction in the US.

#799. FA chief signs NDA to view Fifa sell-off plot documents

Debbie Hewitt has been chair at the FA since 2022

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) as a condition of viewing documents related to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.

Hewitt was granted access to the information at the world governing body's headquarters in Zurich.

Earlier this month, Fifa said "key documents" on the abandoned plan to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors would be made available to members of its council, but only in person and under "strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality".

Uefa had demanded Fifa release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and answer questions relating to its decision-making.

Hewitt was among a group of council members who wrote to Fifa to say they were "concerned that any review would seemingly be limited to certain 'key documents'â¦ which in turn would only be available for review under unknown 'strict review protocols'".

They also asked for clarity on what the protocols were, and "an explanation as to why Fifa considers such restrictions necessary since it is not clear why our rights are being limited in such a way".

The NDA means Hewitt cannot reveal what she has read, or comment about it publicly.

Fair Square, which campaigns for greater accountability in sport, told BBC Sport: "Debbie Hewitt and the FA didn't need to see the details of FFE to know that it was a gross abuse of presidential power.

"As a member association, the FA is entitled to hold the Fifa president accountable for his actions, and as a Fifa Council vice-president, Hewitt should have seen these plans as soon as they were hatched.

"They had the right to demand to see these documents, and should have exercised that right forcefully and publicly, rather than signing a gagging clause that puts Fifa and Infantino back in control."

115 days, 39 private-jet flights, one election - Infantino's globetrotting

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

Hewitt has previously criticised Infantino for a lack of transparency.

However, she embraced the Fifa president at a ceremony in Zurich on Monday when the UK bid to host the 2035 Women's World Cup was ratified at a special ceremony.

It is unclear whether she viewed the files on the same day, and which documents have been made available.

Last week, BBC Sport revealed the FA had considered challenging Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, and that it is backing French candidate Philippe Diallo in next year's presidential election.

Fifa has been approached for comment. Sources have previously indicated Fifa's ability to answer some questions is limited by legal action that Uefa launched in October in the US, requesting disclosure of evidence and documents, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

Dane Cook and Kelsi Taylor—who tied the knot in 2023—shared that she is pregnant with their first baby: “We’ve been bursting with excitement to share this news!”

Dane Cook is preparing for his chapter as dad of the month.

The comedian and wife Kelsi Taylor shared they are expecting their first baby together.

Alongside black-and-white maternity photos, Cook, 54, and Taylor, 28, wrote in a joint Nov. 24 Instagram post that they’ve “been bursting with excitement to share this news!”

They added in reference to a bible verse about an answered prayer for a baby, “1 Samuel 1:27.”

In the first snap, the Good Luck Chuck star and fitness inductor stood beneath a tree as they looked lovingly into each other’s eyes. Meanwhile, Taylor held up a sonagram of their baby as Cook laid a gentle hand on her wrist.

Showing off their playful side, another photo showed the couple cozied up on a couch, while a third picture captured a close-up of Taylor’s baby bump.

Reposting the carousel to her Instagram Stories, Taylor wrote, “So grateful for this beautiful chapter of our lives.”

And Cook would have to agree, sharing on his own Instagram Stories that he’s “feeling so incredible.”

The Employee of the Month alum and Taylor tied the knot in September 2023 at a private estate in O'ahu, Hawaii, after nearly six years of dating.

"Last night I married the girl of my dreams here in Hawaii," Cook shared the day after the wedding on X. "The greatest feeling in the world is knowing you've got the strongest person you could ever imagine by your side and giving them all of your love in return."

He continued, "The years of laughs, adventures and accomplishments we've shared were solidified in front of some of our dearest friends and family during an emotional ceremony. I can't wait to share more but for now just know this. I've never felt this way. It's so wonderful."

It’s also wonderful that the couple can poke fun at their 27-year age gap. In fact, the My Best Friend’s Girl actor included a few wisecracks about their relationship in his 2022 stand-up special Dane Cook: Above It All.

"She saw everything that I was working on for the show," Cook exclusively told E! News at the special’s premiere. "And she was like, ‘Keep that in. I think that part will be great.' There's even some fun at our own expense."

As for why he wanted to draw inspiration from their age difference? "If we can't laugh at it,” he said, "then nobody else is allowed."

And that wasn’t going to fly with Cook. After all, he hopes to keep laughing at every twist and turn his life takes.

"I think it'll change it in the way that I would always hope growing up with a generation of comedy fans,” he explained. “I was a college kid talking to college-age students. And to grow up with a generation of comedy fans, their kids are now coming to my show. I'm family oriented and to be looking at that with Kelsey and our future and family. They’re not the only stars who’ve been candid about their age-gap romance. Keep reading for more…

Sam Taylor-Johnson & Aaron Taylor-Johnson

The yoga instructor has admitted she used to judge couples with big age gaps before her relationship with the actor, who is 26 years her senior."Alec and I are on all the lists of 'Celebrities with the Biggest Age Differences' and stuff like that," she explained on her podcast Witches Anonymous in 2022. Probably so over it."I totally get the judgment initially, but things are never as they appear," Katharine said on Dr. Berlin's Informed Pregnancy Podcast in 2023. One thing that’s not unwritten? #797. Oxford beat Spurs U21s to seal EFL Trophy progress

Aaron Ramsey is experiencing the EFL Trophy for the first time in his football career

Aaron Ramsey's Oxford United beat Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1 to secure one of the final two Jersey Mike's Trophy knockout spots.

Oxford knew avoiding defeat by a margin of four goals or more would be enough to seal progression from Southern Group A alongside already-qualified Exeter City.

They trailed to Tyler Tingey's early opener on Tuesday, which gave Spurs' youngsters a glimmer of hope of pulling off that mini-miracle.

But Jun'ai Byfield's own goal and 18-year-old Jack Lee's late winner ensured ex-Arsenal man Ramsey got one over his old north London rivals as Oxford won to finish top of the group.

Elsewhere, Fleetwood's decisive Northern Group G match at home to Leeds United Under-21s was put back 24 hours because of a waterlogged pitch.

The two sides will now meet on Wednesday to decide who progresses alongside group leaders Oldham Athletic to complete the line-up for the knockout stages.

There were wins for League Two pair Tranmere Rovers and Salford City over Premier League sides in Tuesday's other two ties, which were virtually dead rubbers.

Tranmere, who had already sealed their last-32 spot, came from behind to beat eliminated Everton Under-21s 2-1 with goals from David Kamara and Charlie Veevers in Northern Group E.

Both Salford City and Sunderland Under-21s had already been eliminated from Northern Group A but goals from Paolo Mariani, Brandon Cooper and Kyrell Malcolm gave the Ammies a 3-2 win despite Jaydon Jones' Black Cats double.

Of the 16 Premier League under-21 sides to enter the competition, with one placed in each group, only six have progressed to the knockout rounds, although Leeds can still make that number seven.

The last-32 draw will take place on Wednesday at 16:30 GMT. Ties will take place in the week commencing 7 December.

All 16 group winners are guaranteed a home tie, with fixtures remaining regionalised until the semi-final stage.

#796. Arsenal punished for bluntless in attack - but Man City also have problems

Arsenal and Man City both slipped up in the Champions League in midweek ahead of their big Premier League meeting this weekend; watch Arsenal vs Man City live on Sky Sports Premier League this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm

By Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium, Adam Bate at the Etihad Stadium

Arsenal face Manchester City in a blockbuster Premier League contest this weekend, but in recent days and months, both teams have issues to overcome.

Arsenal have drawn back-to-back games against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund, with Mikel Arteta's side throwing away comfortable half-time leads in both matches.

City, meanwhile, come into the game on a run of just one win in their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

The game could have a huge impact on the Premier League title race, with Arsenal hoping to open up a nine-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side, who in turn could close the gap to the reigning champions to just three points with a win.

Sky Sports reporters Sam Blitz and Adam Bate were at Arsenal and City's draws in midweek and analyse their respective issues...

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium:

Arsenal have the most 1-0 wins out of any Premier League team since Mikel Arteta took over the club in December 2019. It's all well and good - until teams start making it 1-1.

And in the last two games, they have. And Arsenal only have themselves to blame.

After the Gunners' 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, Arteta was convinced that their recent draws against Newcastle and the Bundesliga leaders are not comparable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

He claims Arsenal played well in this Champions League stalemate - and repeated on several occasions that Dortmund benefited from an "element of luck". There's an element of truth to that - the woodwork was struck three times in the second half.

But Arsenal had thirty shots against Dortmund - the most they've ever had in a Champions League game. Just four of those shots were on target. Seven shots came from within the six-yard box, no goals came from them.

And it's costing them points. Because there has been a pattern in Arsenal's last two matches. Dominate the first half, only take a 1-0 lead, start the second half slowly and then end up drawing the game.

Out of the 2.2 worth of Expected Goals Arsenal missed in the game, 0.96 of that tally came in the first half. From their 13 shots that didn't lead to a goal, they should have taken a bigger advantage.

It invited Dortmund back into the contest when there shouldn't have been one in the first place. Like Newcastle did at the weekend, the Bundesliga leaders sorted their game plan out in the half-time break and came out firing.

Arteta is right that the Newcastle and Dortmund games are different because Arsenal rallied to seize dominance of the game right after the German side's equaliser.

But once again, the conversation sits around the holes in Arsenal's attacking quality, particularly at left wing and up front. After Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus left the club this summer without being replaced, Arsenal are still searching for attacking inspiration at left wing, with neither centre-forward in a goalscoring run of form.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Christos Tzolis is still waiting for his first Arsenal goal, Eberechi Eze is lacking consistency and Viktor Gyokeres backed up his early strike and impressive all-round display by creating doubts again by missing a late sitter.

At the start of the season, Gary Neville questioned whether Arsenal had the attacking player capable of delivering the Champions League. The draw to Dortmund backed that claim up.

Arteta struck a calm and positive tone after the Dortmund draw. It was a figure who knows his team have a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League, and will go on to qualify for the knockout stages of the Champions League.

But if these traits continue, it can all slip away quickly in this busy part of the season. If Arsenal don't beat Real Madrid, their top eight spot will be under threat.

Last season, they also benefited hugely from getting a top two spot that meant the second legs of their entire knockout stages were at the Emirates. PSG and Real can open up a bit of a gap on Arsenal in the coming weeks.

And up next, it's Manchester City at the Emirates. Enzo Maresca's side tend to score in most games. A 1-0 lead may not be enough.

Sky Sports' Adam Bate at the Etihad Stadium:

Move the ball quicker, yelled one fan from behind the press box. Press them, screamed a youngster in front. They were not wrong. Manchester City still have the individual quality to entertain the Etihad Stadium but they are also a frustrating watch at present.

City have picked up just one point from their last four Premier League games and while they did defeat RB Leipzig 3-2 in their previous Champions League outing, they let in two more in this draw with Napoli. It is 10 games now without keeping a clean sheet.

"Off the ball, the team was good from my point of view," said Enzo Maresca in the press conference afterwards, presenting a positive spin. "We did not concede a lot. The problem is that they were clinical. We created many chances." Not everyone agreed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"It is not good enough," City captain Erling Haaland had told TNT Sports just before. "We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want." Tellingly, the striker then added: "When you do not win you start to question everything."

Maresca is being questioned. He has stressed that he is months into his time here not years and it is evident that he is still searching for the solutions. Finding the best role for new signings Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez is something that he is still tweaking.

Against Napoli, it was Jeremy Doku's spark off the bench that helped to bring the first equaliser and Rayan Cherki's class that delivered the second. But it was all the bits in between, with and without the ball, that will concern the Manchester City supporters.

Rasmus Hojlund got the better of Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma as Napoli were rewarded for pressing City high up the pitch. Noa Lang converted Leonardo Spinazzola's right-wing cross on the counter-attack - highlighting another weakness.

Maresca turned on his heels and looked to the skies in exasperation at that one because it is a recurring issue for City. They remain susceptible to the breakaways even when he loads the midfield in attempt to prevent it. Losing duels is another theme.

Sluggishness is an easy accusation. Haaland was largely anonymous, unable to get into the game. But that is because City are yet to find a pressing structure that works for them. Even if Haaland does close down, his team-mates are not necessarily following.

As had happened against Fulham at the weekend, Napoli were able to have good possession of the ball, something that was once unheard of for visiting teams at this stadium. That aura was already fading under Pep Guardiola but it is truly absent now.

Maresca is an excellent coach and the structure at Manchester City remains such that he can expect to be given time to figure all this out. But as he himself has previously acknowledged, there is not just one thing that is undermining this team right now.

The loss at Aston Villa was not the same as the home reverse to Brighton. Fulham approached it very differently to Nottingham Forest. Both got results. And now Napoli, in just one game, showed two different ways to undo Maresca's side. Problems to solve.

#795. See Kristen Stewart’s Out of This World Transformation into Sally Ride

Kristen Stewart looked straight out of the 1980s as she transformed into famed NASA astronaut Sally Ride on the set of the upcoming limited series The Challenger.

Where the hell has Kristen Stewart been, loca?

Well, in short, outer space. For the Twilight actress’ latest role as groundbreaking NASA astronaut Sally Ride—a.k.a. the first American woman to fly in space—in The Challenger, she fully changed up her look, rocking a look straight out of the ‘80s.

Stewart donned a brunette bob on the Georgia set of the Prime Video limited series Nov. 24, completing her look with a 1980s style shirt—tied with a bow at the collar—and a dark pair of bottoms. The 36-year-old kept warm on set with a fluffy zip-up sweater as she sipped on a Diet Coke between takes.

The role marks the Oscar nominee’s first regular TV role, with her also serving as a producer on the series alongside wife Dylan Meyers through their production company Nevermind Pictures.

And for Stewart, she couldn’t believe she had the chance to bring Ride’s story to life.

“I’m shaking in boots, but I get to play Sally Ride,” she shared with Collider in December. “The story is incredible and the team is just so inspired and trustworthy and I think I'm in the safest hands.”

The limited series is inspired by Meredith E. Bagby’s 2023 book The New Guys, which chronicled the story of Ride and her fellow astronauts who all broke barriers as NASA’s 1978 astronaut class.

In addition to being the first American woman—and third woman—to fly in space in 1983, Ride also served on the committees that investigated the explosions of the Space Shuttle Challenger in 1986 and the Space Shuttle Columbia in 2003, making her the only person to participate in both.

While she was married to fellow astronaut Steven Hawley from 1982 to 1987, Ride was in a long term relationship with women’s tennis star Tam O’Shaughnessy from 1985 until her death in 2012 from pancreatic cancer at the age of 61. However, Ride hid the fact that she was part of the LGBTQ community during her lifetime, with the news only coming out when O’Shaughnessy was noted to have been her partner of 27 years in her obituary.

Following her death, O’Shaughnessy spoke about the couple’s time together, sharing that while Ride never officially came out to her family, they were all still very accepting of the couple’s relationship.

“Sally never verbally, openly told her mother, her father, or her sister, Bear, that she was gay and that we were a couple. But Sally never hid it from them,” she explained to the Windy City Times in 2013, “you know, I went everywhere with Sally, and she went everywhere with me.”

“Her parents are really smart—especially her mother and her sister,” the former tennis pro added, “they knew a long time ago that we were a couple.”

#794. Palace docked points for using four sub windows in WSL win

Scottish striker Kirsty Howat signed for Crystal Palace in September 2025

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points after using too many substitution windows during their win on the opening day of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season.

Palace, who were playing their first match following promotion back to the WSL, beat Everton 1-0 on 6 September at Gander Green Lane.

However, manager Jo Potter brought on Kirsty Howat for Shannon O'Brien in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to try and shore up the victory.

It was the fourth separate substitution made by Potter, who had also made changes in the 62nd, 83rd and 90th minutes.

While WSL managers are allowed to make five changes in a game, they must be made across only three stoppages in play to avoid excessive time wasting.

Crystal Palace deducted points following WSL win

Palace have been stripped of the three points they earned in the match - one of only two WSL games the Eagles have won this season.

This punishment drops Palace down one place in the WSL table to 13th - the relegation play-off place.

Palace are now below fellow promoted side Birmingham City in the table on goal difference, with both sides now having six points - six behind Everton in 11th.

In a statement on their club website, external Palace said they were "disappointed" by the decision.

The decision was made by an independent tribunal after Palace admitted the breach of competition rule 5.19.1.

The rule states: "A substitution can only be made when play is stopped for any reason and the referee has given permission. A club at its discretion may use five substitute players during a match. For the avoidance of doubt, each club has no more than three substitution opportunities in each match."

The tribunal said that while the rule breach was inadvertent and "not intended to secure an unfair advantage", it said a points deduction was necessary in order to provide a deterrent to clubs against making a similar mistake in future.

"The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained, save in exceptional circumstances," the tribunal stated in its full written decision., external

They said the lateness of the substitution in the match - so late that Howat did not touch the ball after coming on - did not excuse Palace from punishment.

It also ruled "that responsibility for complying with the rule rests with clubs, not match officials".

Palace - who placed the word "fourth" in inverted commas in their response to the ruling - are aiming to improve on their only previous WSL campaign in 2024-25, where they only won twice in 22 matches and were relegated by a 10-point margin.

Their statement read: "Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty â a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.

"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL."

Forward Lexi Lloyd-Smith had scored the only goal of the game in the 34th minute on her Palace debut.

#793. Why Potts swapped West Ham for Club Brugge after 16 years

Freddie Potts has started all of Club Brugge's Champions League games

When Liverpool visit Club Brugge on Wednesday they are likely to come up against English midfielder Freddie Potts.

The 23-year-old ended a 16-year association with West Ham in the summer to join the Belgian champions for an undisclosed fee.

And he has started every game, bar one missed through suspension, in all competitions.

After losing to Aston Villa in the Champions League, they have defeated Inter Milan, Lens and PSV.

"It really is a dream because you hear the music and then you see your family in the stands and you remember all the times that you watched Champions League on TV," Potts told BBC Radio 5 Live's Euro Leagues Show.

"You think of all the memories that you make watching it and to be playing in it now is something that every kid dreams of."

Potts' whole life had been based around West Ham. He had been with the club since the age of six and his father Steve, who made 506 appearances for the Hammers, is a first-team coach.

Potts Jr played 28 times for West Ham, with 25 of them coming last season as they were relegated from the Premier League.

He also had loan spells with Wycombe in League One and Portsmouth in the Championship.

"In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren't as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said 'let's explore options because this season I'm 22, turning 23'," Potts said.

"It's a massive part of my career and I wanted to play. The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn't really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

"I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.

"It was an emotional decision because it had to be made quite quickly. It's been the right decision for me and so far I'm enjoying it, I'm loving life here."

Club Brugge won the Belgian title last season and are second, just one point behind leaders Union Saint-Gilloise this campaign.

"It's a physical league," said Potts. "My running and physical stats have been higher than they've ever been. It's a demanding league in that way.

"Club Brugge demands a lot, from winning the ball back and going man for man in the press. And your responsibility off the ball is something that you have to take really seriously."

Freddie Potts on leaving West Ham, life in Belgium and beating Inter Milan

Potts says he has not started to learn French or Flemish and that team talks are done in English, with the side managed by Croat Ivan Leko.

And he revealed he has a lifelong history with the city.

"The whole move itself is funny because we used to visit Brugge when I was a kid," he said.

"We used to come around Christmas, so my family all know the city. And now I'm here they come out as much as they can.

"It's a great city with a lot of culture. It's brilliant. You won't find many places like it."

Next up for the side is the visit of Liverpool this week - with both clubs on nine points after four games.

The Reds are eighth and Club Brugge are ninth in the table.

"Everyone knows Liverpool as a club, the size and the Premier League teams," said Potts, who started for West Ham at home to the Reds last season.

"It's going to be a big game. We're level on points in the Champions League and we've put big performances in this competition and we're hoping that we're going to do the same."

#792. 90 Day Fiancé Alum Sheila Mangubat's Cause of Death Revealed

After 90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days alum Sheila Mangubat died at age 35, sign language interpreter Aimee Adiwang, who worked with the couple, shared her cause of death.

New details about Sheila Mangubat's private health battle have come to light.

After the 90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days alum's former fiancé David Dangerfield confirmed she had died at 35, the cause has been revealed.

Mangubat and Dangerfield's sign language interpreter Aimee Adiwang shared with Page Six in a Nov. 24 statement that the reality star died suddenly after a battle with a gynecological cancer at age 35 in the Philippines.

Adiwang—who worked with the pair since Dangerfield was born deaf and used sign language to communicate—did not specify the cancer she was diagnosed with. Mangubat's niece had also told her that her aunt had suffered from a urinary tract infection (UTI) prior to her death.

The interpreter reflected on their time working together during season six of the 90 Day spinoff in an emotional Instagram tribute alongside screengrabs from the 2023 episode.

Even though these are one of the few photos we have together," Adiwang wrote on Instagram Nov. 23. "I'm holding onto them tightly as I remember where our friendship began. Honoring her life and the warmth she brought into mine as she rests peacefully with the Lord."

She concluded, "I will always be grateful for her presence in my life."

Dangerfield initially shared the news in an emotional Instagram message Nov. 22, noting that the family of Mangubat—whom he split from in October 2025 due to distance and K-1 visa issues, but eventually began dating again in June, according to TMZ—told him about her death.

"I am devastated and still trying to process this loss," he continued. "Please keep her son, her family, and me in your prayers. Thank you for all your love and support."

Although their romance had its ups and downs, the 45-year-old only had love for Mangubat, who leaves behind son Jhonreil from a previous relationship.

"I'm happy I never gave up because I found my love," he said on a June 2023 episode. "I have a girlfriend whose name is Sheila, and she's beautiful."

"When I first saw Sheila's picture, it got my heart beating," he continued. "I will have a new family with Sheila in the future. Sheila is better than any other woman I've dated because Sheila is a sweet person. She is the perfect match to me. I'll love Sheila forever."

#790. ‘The worst COP ever’ offers a chance to learn from failure

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Protesters on the final day of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey. Credit: Chris McGrath/Getty

‘The worst COP ever’ is how some people have described the United Nations COP31 climate meeting in Antalya, Turkey, which ended on 22 November. COP31 was the first to take place after the confirmation that global warming will overshoot the safe limit of 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels. Despite a two-day extension to the meeting and several proposals for an overarching political declaration or ‘cover decision’, delegates left after two weeks of talks without such an agreement.

The world’s first plastics treaty is in crisis: can it be salvaged?

The world’s first plastics treaty is in crisis: can it be salvaged?

Drafted by the host nations (Turkey and Australia, this year), a cover decision is a statement that all countries can agree on at the end of the talks. It is not a legally binding text and is a relatively recent innovation. That participants failed to agree such a statement is not a surprise. It requires a willingness for give and take, which was in short supply because many of the countries that attended this year are at war, subject to economic and other sanctions, or involved in trade disputes. Furthermore, the United States, the world’s biggest economy and the largest historic carbon emitter, did not attend following its withdrawal from the COP process.

Delegates from the world’s poorest countries were angry that there was no mention of concrete measures to increase finance for climate adaptation — money that they will need to help them to become more resilient to climate shocks. Many delegates were also angry that the draft text did not include any reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels. Previous cover decisions have included such language, overcoming objections from fossil-fuel-producing states. This time, however, delegates from these states were more determined to block such wording.

But there are key reasons why it would be wrong to conclude that such climate conferences have outlived their purpose — or that a consensus-based approach should be abandoned, as some have argued. There is always room to improve, but COP meetings are much more than what happens in the final days when high-level political representatives turn up.

Environmental treaties are paralysed — here’s how we can do better

Environmental treaties are paralysed — here’s how we can do better

First, these meetings mainly involve discussions between technical experts and observers — including many researchers — representing the countries that have signed up to the UN’s climate agreement, known as the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change. For most of the two weeks (and in many timetabled talks before a COP), delegates meet in working groups to discuss a spectrum of climate-change topics. The Antalya meeting discussions included how to accelerate electrification, cut methane emissions and mobilize new finance to protect the world’s forests. Progress in these technical talks is often incremental. In contrast to the final days of a COP, which are organized around negotiations between political representatives, expert delegates focus on getting things done rather than posturing.

The second reason not to write off this COP is that it’s not uncommon for countries to leave meetings without a high-level agreement. Indeed, some previous ‘good’ outcomes needed earlier COP meetings to ‘fail’. The landmark COP21 Paris climate agreement signed in 2015, a legally binding text in which nations agreed to limit global warming to 1.5 °C, is perhaps the best-known example. In 2009, COP15 in Copenhagen resulted in deadlock. That failure prompted deeper thinking and discussions at subsequent COP meetings on the steps needed for the world to stay within safe climate limits, laying the groundwork for the Paris agreement.

Still, the current geopolitical climate is a substantial obstacle to progress, affecting not only COP climate meetings but also talks on other international agreements, such as a proposed treaty to end plastic pollution. Another set of talks occurring at the same time as COP31 — on setting international restrictions on autonomous weapons — also failed to reach an agreement and will resume in 2028.

In the case of both the climate and plastics talks, a relatively small group of countries — including Iran, Russia and Saudi Arabia, which are heavily reliant on fossil-fuel exports, among others — are blocking stronger action. Some researchers, as well as country delegates, say that the UN’s method of decision-making (that all countries must agree a consensus) is the problem, and question whether there should instead be a vote and a decision made by majority.

Trust and science: the essential elements missing from plastics treaty talks

Trust and science: the essential elements missing from plastics treaty talks

There is some logic in changing the approach for the cover decisions to avoid the overtly self-interested blocking of action. But for many other decisions made at UN climate and other environment-related meetings, abandoning a consensus-based approach in favour of a vote would not be a good option.

The UN’s expert groups for example, including the scientists who are part of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (which synthesizes studies to inform decisions), must continue to work through consensus. Delegates painstakingly review, debate and discuss evidence, before coming to a conclusion — and it is important that all those involved are brought in at this point.

A change to voting might, in some cases, mean faster results, but it would also undermine the principles that everyone owns the result and that global problems need global solutions.

It is right that, on reflecting on the COP in Antalya, many will ask what needs to change. And some aspects must. But altering how decisions are made should not be taken lightly. Climate change doesn’t respect borders. It won’t be solved by countries working on their own or in small groups.

#789. Britt Stewart's Ultimate Guide to "Thoughtful & Curated" Holiday Gifts

DWTS' Britt Stewart is not only a great dancer, but a very thoughtful holiday gift giver! She exclusively revealed to E! her intentional tricks and gift ideas to help you win the holiday season.

The last thing anyone wants for the holidays is a gift that feels impersonal! To avoid giving something to your loved ones that they'll just toss to the side and not actually appreciate, it's time to get serious with your gift-giving this year.

Ahead of the Dancing With the Stars season 35 finale, E! exclusively chatted with pro Britt Stewart, who is not only a dancer with moves we envy, but a very intentional gift giver:

"I’ll always choose giving an experience over things because creating memories with the people I love most is incredibly important to me," she told us. "If I chose to gift something physical, it has to be thoughtful and curated specifically for the person receiving it. As a self-care advocate, my favorite gifts are the ones that remind people to pause, reset, and take a little time for themselves."

And as for her favorite part of celebrating the holiday season, it's building holiday memories with her husband, actor and her former DWTS partner, Daniel Durant.

"For me, the best part of celebrating the holidays is spending quality time with my family. My husband Daniel and I got married last August and we’re still creating what our own holiday traditions look like, which makes it extra special. I also love that the end of the year gives us all a genuine reason to slow down, be present with the people we love most and reflect on the past year," she shared.

Scroll on for all of Britt's thoughtful gift ideas and tips, including her Los Angeles favorites, just in time for the holidays.

Do you have any current favorites in your beauty routine that you think would make great holiday gifts for beauty lovers?

"My favorite beauty tool right now is the Therabody Face depuffing wand, which cools and heats, and is one of my favorite things to do during my morning rituals. I put on a daily sheet mask and use the cool setting first to help my face depuff, then switch to the heated setting to help the serum really penetrate my skin. It is a must have and would make an amazing gift for the beauty and skin care enthusiasts in your life."

This celeb-loved depuffing tool has cold and heat treatments to help reduce under-eye puffiness, enhance radiance and diminish the look of dark circles.

What’s a gift you’ve received that you get so much use out of?

"One of the best parts about gift-giving is getting someone something they wouldn’t normally buy for themselves, but actually really need. My husband Daniel is always up to date on the latest technology, so last year he gifted me a new laptop. It was something I hadn’t done for myself in over ten years, and it’s a gift that I use on a daily basis!"

Lightweight and portable, this MacBook is available in four different colors, each with a vibrant 13-inch display.

"Not every gift needs to be as big as a new laptop and sometimes gifts that are inspired by a conversation with a friend mean so much! I have organized Secret Santa for the Dancing with the Stars Live tour cast for the past couple years, and one year Emma Slater gave me a productivity and idea building journal. It was so intentional, as she knew how much I love journaling, but picked something specifically aligned with a goal I had at that time."

This productivity planner by Papier has space to plan and track your goals, with pages for monthly, weekly and daily planning.

If you were going to a white elephant gift exchange with your fellow DWTS pros - what would you bring and why?

"For my fellow pros, I would bring a gift card for a massage. We all put ourselves through so much both physically and mentally and a massage would be the perfect gift that we all need! I’d specifically choose The NOW Massage, which is a local favorite here in the Los Angeles area, and gift them their specific signature treatment called The Stretch."

For those not in L.A., give them a gift of a massage at home! This jojoba oil-based massage candle is full of skin-loving ingredients.

This body brush is made with copper bristles, ideal for using before a massage or luxurious bath to remove dead skin and boost circulation.

What’s your go-to host/hostess gift when attending holiday gatherings?

"If you want to step away from the usual bottle of wine or bouquet of flowers, I love finding a nice and unique bottle of olive oil as the perfect holiday gift. Everyone needs a good bottle of olive oil in their kitchen! Flamingo Estate, a local company here in Los Angeles that ships nationwide, is such a great brand for this. They also have produce boxes filled with seasonal produce and curated gift boxes, which is another gift option that is fresh and unique."

This Flamingo Estate trio is perfect for anyone who loves to cook, or has it on their list of resolutions for 2027. It includes the brand's olive oil, plus wildflower honey and salsa macha.

You spend a lot of time on the road for DWTS tour - what are some must-haves you always bring that a travel lover might appreciate for a holiday gift?

"A must-have for traveling are my packing cubes. I love to stay organized and I have a place for almost everything, so packing cubes for your clothes and a nice travel toiletry bag are always the way to go for anyone who travels a lot."

Available in multiple sizes and colors, the packing cubes by BÉIS fit seamlessly into their bestselling luggage, with labels to help you stay organized for any trip.

"I also always travel with a candle. Being away from home for long periods of time has taught me that even something as small as a candle can make an environment feel cozy and a little bit more like home."

Can't get enough of Flamingo Estate? This luxe candle includes notes of vanilla, cypress, guaiac and green vanilla.

What are some holiday gift ideas for newlyweds?

"Tying back to my love for experiences over material gifts, giving newlyweds a fun activity or memorable experience they can do together is such an amazing way to help them make new memories and stay connected. With how busy Daniel and I are, carving out time to create memories together is something we hold really close to our hearts. For our first anniversary, my mom secretly paid for our dinner and we only found out afterward. Those little surprises and thoughtful touches go a long way whatever stage of your relationship you’re in."

Turn a happy memory from their wedding day into a fun activity with this photo puzzle, which can be framed and hung at home!

"If you lean more towards sentimental gifts, finding something unique to your relationship and turning it into a keepsake is always so special. #788. 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?

When the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border. Yet, 37 years later, many people on both sides remain deeply skeptical of each other.

Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

We asked three artists from Germany with different perspectives on the history of the country's division to share their views.

Author Lea Streisand was born in 1979 and experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall firsthand while growing up in East Berlin.

In her books and essays, she has returned to her East German upbringing many times, using literature to process it.

The novel "Hufeland, at the corner of Bötzow" (2019, Ullstein), for example, recounts the period of reunification from a child's perspective.

"November 9, 1989, was simply incredible," she told DW. She was 10 years old at the time. When her mother bought her winter boots with the 100 Deutsche Marks she received from the West German state — a welcome gift given to all East German citizens — she was so disappointed that she felt like crying. But later, a friend of her parents' let her buy so many sweets at the supermarket that they lasted until Christmas.

"The disappointment really set in afterwards, with what happened over the course of the following year. It was unbelievable how quickly an entire system was suddenly swept away and a new one built up, as if to say, 'There you go. You're welcome'," Streisand recalled. "I think it was just too fast for people."

The people of East Germany, or the GDR, had brought about the fall of the Berlin Wall themselves through a civil rights movement and numerous demonstrations. For many, however, the goal was not to dissolve the state immediately but to reform it.

Among them was Anke Feuchtenberger, born in 1963 in East Berlin. Her childhood was spent in East Berlin and in the East German region of Western Pomerania, where she now lives again and feels "very much at home."

Today, she teaches at the University of Applied Sciences in Hamburg, meaning she spends time on both sides of the former divide. Feuchtenberger is often described as Germany's most influential comic artist. Her work has also garnered international acclaim.

"Back then, as artists, we tried to bring about a change through posters and flyers — to gain more freedom without immediately abolishing socialism," she explained.

At the time, the fall of the Berlin Wall stirred up mixed feelings in Feuchtenberger: "I soon realized that the creative and revolutionary aspects of our movement were very quickly being smothered by consumerism, and that nationalist tendencies — which had already been noticeable before — were coming to the fore," Feuchtenberger recalled. "That made me afraid."

Meanwhile, for photographic artist Simon Menner, born in 1978 in Emmendingen, in the West German state of Baden-Württemberg, Berlin was very far away. As Menner put it, he experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child in a "rather abstract" way. Today, Berlin is his home.

In his experience, the way films and documentaries portrayed East Germany around the time of reunification was very bleak. "But West Germany in the '80s," he said, "was also bleak and very staid."

This uneven portrayal of the two parts of Germany is an issue that deeply concerns Menner — partly because he unwittingly contributed to it in a small way. Among other things, Menner's work explores the topic of surveillance and how it works.

In the archives of East Germany's Ministry for State Security, or Stasi — which are freely accessible today as part of the National Archives — he discovered a massive collection of photographs that both fascinated and horrified him and which he wanted to bring to the attention of a wider public.

His photo book "Top Secret" (2012, from publisher Hatje Cantz) features a selection of photos that offer a unique insight into the work of the Stasi. Some are eerie, while others are curious or even absurd.

Menner also tried to look into the photo archive of West Germany's Federal Intelligence Service. "I spent a year trying to gain access — without success," he said.

In hindsight, he now finds his artistic project problematic because he believes it is too one-sided, focusing exclusively on East Germany's past.

According to Menner, West Germany's intelligence services in the 1960s were not exactly models of virtue either, and he believes it is "actually high time" to critically examine this part of history as well. In his view, an honest examination of Germany's past as a whole is a prerequisite for genuine reconciliation.

Streisand believes literature can help foster mutual understanding. "Literature opens a window into experiences we haven't had ourselves," she said. "You can immerse yourself in the mind of someone who has had a different life than you have and understand what happened."

Interest in these stories remains strong. In 2023, Feuchtenberger published the nearly 500-page graphic novel "Comrade Cuckoo" (published by Reprodukt), which was the first graphic novel to be nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize in the fiction category.

The story spans a childhood in the fictional East German village of Pritschitanow in the 1960s in the GDR to the post-Reunification era. In it, Feuchtenberger weaves autobiographical memories of her upbringing with fantastical and fictional elements.

The artist said she was surprised "that, so long after the fall of the wall, my stories have sparked such great interest in the West."

In particular, the fact that the main character, Kerstin, rarely sees her parents because they both work full-time is a topic that often comes up at readings. In the GDR, everyone had the right to work, she said. At the same time, it was a civic duty.

Could the West German interest in this stem from the fact that full-time employment for both parents has long been less common in the West? It's possible, said Feuchtenberger.

When looking toward their shared future, the two East German women are more optimistic than Menner, from West Germany.

"In Berlin, I often don't even notice anymore whether I'm in the West or the East," said Menner. "But when it comes to sociopolitical issues, politicians should listen to older and younger people more closely," he added, referring to the recent election successes of far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD . "Otherwise, things are going to get difficult in the near future."

"It's very important to step outside our own bubble because people all over the world are facing problems. Constantly focusing on this German-German divide that has emerged between the groups doesn't help," said Feuchtenberger.

"For me personally, the whole issue of borders has somehow dissolved," she explained. This is due in no small part to the many trips abroad that have taken her to various places around the world.

Moreover, in her hometown near the Polish border, she observes how animals couldn't care less about the border. "They come from the east and the west and do whatever they want," she said. That's why she also gave "Comrade Cuckoo" the working title "A German Animal in a German Forest," "because I found the absurdity of an animal having a nationality so funny."

"This East-West thing — our children won't have any interest in it at all," said Streisand. "Young people don't care where their parents come from. Can I get a job that will support a family? Do I have to go to war? Right now, completely different things are relevant."

This article was originally written in German.

#786. Steven Hack, Broadway Star and American Horror Story Actor, Dead at 68

Broadway star Steven Hack—also known for roles on shows like Seinfeld, General Hospital and American Horror Story—has died at age 68.

A bright light in Hollywood has gone dim.

Broadway star Steven Hack, who also had minor roles in American Horror Story and Seinfeld, has died after suffering a medical emergency, Los Angeles’ Interact Theatre Company confirmed. He was 68.

“It is with great sadness that we share the news that Steven Hack, a founding member of Interact Theatre Company, recently passed away at home following a sudden and unexpected cardiac event,” the company wrote in a recent statement shared to Instagram. “Steven was a gifted and versatile performer, a superb graphic artist, and a cherished member of our artistic family.”

Hack died of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, according to the County of Los Angeles Medical Examiner, a condition caused by plaque buildup in the arterial walls, per the America Heart Association.

“His creativity and talent helped shape Interact in its earliest years,” the statement continued, “and his artistry, humor, warmth, and generous spirit enriched everything he touched.”

Hack was born in St. Louis in 1958 before going on to study at the California Institute of the Arts and the American Academy of Dramatic Arts.

“Steven took great pride in his early career as a Broadway dancer, which included performing in the original production of CATS and touring with A Chorus Line,” Interact Theatre Company noted. “Here in Los Angeles, he went on to work extensively in film, television, and commercials.”

In fact, he made his screen debut as one of the teenage dancers in the 1978 film Grease before landing roles in other films like Fantastic Four, Thor: The Dark World and The Happytime Murders.

He also dominated the small screen with credits in American Horror Story: 1984, Marvel’s Agent Carter, Criminal Minds, The Newsroom, Days of Our Lives, The West Wing, Scrubs, General Hospital, Seinfeld and so many more.

“As we remember Steven, we celebrate not only his many contributions to our company, but also the joy of knowing and working with him,” Interact Theatre Company wrote. “He will always hold a special place in Interact’s history and in the hearts of those who knew him.”

They expressed hope that Hack’s "memory be a blessing,” adding, "We extend our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, and all who loved him.”
